successors.note: Wadi Rabah infobox "Followed by: Ghassulian"; Wadi Rabah ends c. 4500 BC and the Ghassulian begins c. 4400 BC, so the handover is placed at 4400 BCE.

correction.text: "limited regions of northern Israel and northern Jordan": Sha'ar HaGolan by the Yarmuk, Munhata and Hamadiya in the central Jordan Valley, 'Ain Ghazal (Jordan), "as far north as Byblos, Lebanon", the Habashan Street site in Tel Aviv

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Yarmukian, "a Pottery Neolithic A (PNA) culture of the ancient Levant", infobox "Dates: 6400-6000 BC". The culture ends at the project's first year; the five centuries to 5500 BCE belong to the undated Lodian (Jericho IX) and Nizzanim cultures that "existed alongside" it, so the Yarmukian shape is carried forward at low confidence. No area figure to compare.

correction.text: the "Southern Levant" of the Wadi Rabah culture: Wadi Rabah, Dan, Sepphoris, Yizre'el, Tel Yosef, Ein el-Jarba, Munhata, Lod, Tell es-Sultan (Jericho), Atlit Yam, Teluliot Batashi

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Wadi Rabah culture, infobox "c. 5500 BC - 4500 BC", "a Pottery Neolithic/ Early Chalcolithic archaeological culture of the Southern Levant"; the lead dates it to "the middle of the 5th millennium BCE". Kenyon's "Pottery Neolithic B" at Jericho is "synonymous with the modernly defined Early Chalcolithic".

region.text: "limited regions of northern Israel and northern Jordan": Sha'ar HaGolan by the Yarmuk, Munhata and Hamadiya in the central Jordan Valley, 'Ain Ghazal (Jordan), "as far north as Byblos, Lebanon", the Habashan Street site in Tel Aviv

ledger.note: 6000 BCE: the Yarmukian villages of the Jordan valley, the first potters of the Levant, open the map. Infobox "Dates: 6400-6000 BC"; "20 other Yarmukian sites have been identified in Israel, Palestine, Jordan and Lebanon"; the culture "derives its name from the Yarmuk River, which flows near its type site". It ends at the project's first year; the dossier carries the Pottery Neolithic forward.

5500 BCE: the Wadi Rabah culture replaces the Yarmukian-Lodian Pottery Neolithic. Wadi Rabah infobox "c. 5500 BC - 4500 BC"; the Yarmukian infobox "Followed by: Wadi Rabah"; the Lodian and Nizzanim of the intervening centuries are undated on both pages.

region.text: the "Southern Levant" of the Wadi Rabah culture: Wadi Rabah, Dan, Sepphoris, Yizre'el, Tel Yosef, Ein el-Jarba, Munhata, Lod, Tell es-Sultan (Jericho), Atlit Yam, Teluliot Batashi

ledger.note: 4400 BCE: the Ghassulian Chalcolithic succeeds the Wadi Rabah. Wadi Rabah infobox end 4500 BC and "Followed by: Ghassulian"; Tel Tsaf belongs to "the following Early/Middle Chalcolithic period (c. 5300-4500 BCE)"; the Ghassulian infobox begins c. 4400 BC, and the century between is bridged here.

certainty.note: An archaeological culture: a band along the Jordan and radii around excavated sites, never a frontier.

notes: One dossier for the Pottery Neolithic of the southern Levant (6000-4400 BCE), with the Yarmukian-to-Wadi Rabah change as a rename, because neither culture alone covers the span and the Lodian (Jericho IX) and Nizzanim have no dates on the pages. Disagreements: Wadi Rabah 5500-4500 BC (infobox) vs "middle of the 5th millennium" (lead); its end 4500 vs the Ghassulian start 4400. The Pre-Pottery Neolithic (Jericho PPNA/PPNB, 'Ain Ghazal) ended before 6000 BCE and is not drawn. Lebanon beyond Byblos and the Syrian coast are not on the pages. Gazetteer: Sha'ar HaGolan, Munhata, Teleilat Ghassul are not places; "Jordan Valley" is not a region, a 35 km band along the Jordan river is used.
